name: Face-tracking pan-tilt camera
summary: An M5Stack Timer Camera on two SG90 servos that turns to keep a face in the middle of the picture, on a weighted printed base and USB power.

spec.name: Face-Tracking Pan-Tilt Camera
spec.function: Follows a face around the room: the ESP32 camera finds the face in each frame (ESP-WHO face detection, or a laptop running OpenCV over the Wi-Fi stream) and turns a pan servo in the base and a tilt servo in a printed yoke to keep it centred, all from one USB-C supply.
spec.quote: I want a little camera on my desk that follows my face, like the ESP32-CAM pan-tilt builds on Hackster: two SG90s, a printed base and yoke, one USB cable, under 35 euros and 300 grams with the plug. The servos should have at least three times the torque the camera head needs, the USB supply has to cope with both servos stalling while it streams, and it must not tip over when the head swings.

parts.name: Weighted base
parts.description: Round hollow base 100 mm across and 30 mm high centred on X=Y=0 (Z 0 to 30), 2.4 mm walls and a 5 mm floor, with a 23 x 12.8 mm pocket in the top for the pan servo whose shaft is at X=Y=0 and a USB-C cable slot in the +Y wall.

parts.name: Pan yoke
parts.description: U bracket on the pan servo horn: a 50 x 20 x 3 mm plate at Z 32 to 35 and two 3 mm uprights 60 mm high at X=+-23.5, with the tilt axis along X at Z=80.

parts.name: Camera head
parts.description: Cradle for the 48 x 24 x 15 mm camera standing upright with the lens towards -Y, centred on the tilt axis at Z=80, with 3 mm axle stubs into the yoke uprights.

parts.name: ESP32 camera board
parts.description: Finds the face and drives both servos from its HY2.0 port

parts.name: Pan servo
parts.description: Turns the yoke, in the base pocket

parts.name: Tilt servo
parts.description: Tilts the camera head, on the right upright

camera.reason: ESP32 with PSRAM and a 3 MP camera, enough for ESP-WHO face detection; its HY2.0 port gives 5 V and two GPIOs, one per servo. The bare ESP32-CAM the Hackster builds use is out of stock at Berrybase today.

pan-servo.reason: The SG90 every pan-tilt build uses: 1.8 kg cm and 5 V from the same USB supply.

tilt-servo.reason: Same SG90 for the tilt axis; the head weighs about 30 g.

power.reason: A rated 3 A USB-C supply for 7.90 EUR: the camera streaming plus both servos at stall stay under it with room to spare.
